children: Shares of Tenable Holdings fell after the company upsized its private placement of convertible senior notes to $725 million.
The stock slipped 4.4%, to $30.63, midday Friday, but has risen 30% this year.

The company said late Thursday that it had upsized the offering of convertible senior notes due 2031 from $650 million. It said the initial purchasers in the offering would have a 13-day option to buy an additional $75 million worth of notes.
The sale to initial purchasers is expected to close Tuesday.

The company expects to net $705.6 million from the offering and will use the proceeds to pay $58.1 million in costs related to capped call transactions, buy back $170.5 million worth of stock, and fully repay its term loans under its senior secured credit facility, as well as for general corporate purposes.
